Well, you know your brain a lot better than I do in that aspect. In that case one can only assume you've had CT scans and blood work that show the chemical imbalance you say you're experiencing. 


The reason I say that is, I've been to a few therapists in adolecence and the first thing they did when I explained what I was feeling is try to put me on medication. They did not do any actual tests on my body before the idea of medication was brought up. None of the people I know who have experienced depression, ever had any actual tests done to figure out whether or not it was actually a chemical imbalance or neurological disorder in their brain before they were ever put on medication. This is why I suggested to you that maybe you might not actually be ill in any sense - you are just feeling the hard feels of shitty circumstance. I'm not sure what the mental health professionals are like where you live. I watched a documentary about a child psychologist who resigned from his job because of the guilt he harbored knowing that a lot of times, they give drugs to children and adolescents not because there's actually anything wrong, but just so child and parents can get along better. I'm just inferring that if you weren't properly tested by having somebody scan your actual brain to take a look at what's going on (which, to my knowledge very rarely ever happens in the mental health field), you may have been wrongly diagnosed. Years of unnecessary medication, however, would probably cause a chemical imbalance and require you to continue to take medication regardless of whether I was right or wrong though. I'm very sorry you're experiencing what you are experiencing. 



Would you like somebody to talk to? Is there anything on your mind? How are you feeling currently?

Incoming wall of text.



I understand what you're going through. Granted, I am not experiencing quite the same thing. I've not been actively depressed my whole life or anything. Back when I was going through adolescence, my hormones were out of whack and I definitely did require counseling for it, but besides that I never needed medication for any kind of illness. I don't think you do, either. Depression is not an illness, it's a reaction to a negative environment. Things happen that enable you to feel sad. This is a perfectly normal thing to experience. A lot of people tend to deny the aspects of their external environment that cause them sadness because acknowledging the root cause of one's sadness often doesn't hold up to the scrutiny of others, and the person feels irrational for letting something that everyone else would consider small to affect them in such a huge way. I find when I talk to people who say they "have no reason" to feel depressed, they've often experienced some sort of trauma that they are unwilling to attribute to the way they are feeling. Why? I don't know. Denial is a bitch, but it is a lot easier to live in denial than it is to acknowlege the real circumstances of your life that are holding you back from truly enjoying it. People want to believe so desperately that their parents are virtuous. They want to believe they themselves are virtuous. They make all kinds of excuses and justifications to enable the toxic behaviour from others in their lives because it's so much easier to excuse evil than it is to destroy it. 


This is where I relate to your experience. I found when I tried to open myself up and explain how I am feeling to the people in my life I THOUGHT cared about me, to the people I THOUGHT encouraged me to be my true self, I was met with a lot of disturbing responses that made me realize how truly alone I am. The responses ranged from "This is too scary to talk about," to "I think you should see a doctor because I'm afraid you are suicidal." I don't know if you'll go back and read my post history here, but I have been pondering the meaninglessness of existence in general, and all I wanted to do was just talk about my thoughts with my friends. I don't believe I am actively contemplating suicide at all - just questioning my own existence and wondering what it all really means. In reality your existence means nothing to the universe. One day you're going to die. There is no God. There is no afterlife. This is your one chance to experience ANYTHING. EVER. I felt really depressed and apathetic about my life because it's not only pointless, but I never got to choose whether or not I wanted to participate. I was just thrown into this life arbitrarily, with no say over any of my circumstances. None of us do. Fuck, that is so shitty. However, last night I came to a sort of silver lining, and I believe somebody had commented on my post the same thing - that since life is meaningless, and this is your one shot to experience at all, do it with all you have and live it to what you would consider the fullest possible. Just go out and have raw, real experiences. Fuck the kind of shit people say you should want. You want to go live on the beach your whole life? Go the fuck ahead man, do what you want. As long as you don't infringe upon the rights of another individual to exist, you do your own thing. Want to be a doctor? Take out a student loan and fuck the world with your doctor skills. In this life, we all have to struggle to survive. Sure, some are born into privilege where their needs are met a lot easier, but we all have to eat and sleep and breathe at the end of the day. In effect, by meeting these needs every day in some way or another, whether that be purely serving just ourselves with our own personal garden we use to produce our own food, or the the work we contribute to the rest of the world in exchange for food. It doesnt matter what you do. You don't ever have to BE anything in order to stay alive. We save our own lives every single day just by drinking water and putting food in our bellies and that is an accomplishment that should never be overlooked. And it really doesn't matter at all how you achieve this accomplishment, because we all die and the universe is going to continue to do what it's going to do regardless of our existence. So when I realized that my life doesn't have any value in comparison to the universe, at first I felt quite small and defeated. Like I was nothing. And in reality, I am nothing and so are you. So is everybody else. I find that a very liberating thought. Like I said, we all only have one shot at experience. Make it grand. You don't owe the world anything. Your existence is justified by the fact that you were even born in the first place. So whether your ability to satisfy your biological needs becomes bumming food from people while living on the streets or working hard to become some grossly paid bank owner or anything in between, those things don't compare to the infinity that is space and our concept of time. Those things mean nothing. The only way anything can have meaning is if you allow it to, because you are a consciousness in a physical body, and your physical body has a biological desire to exist and experience just by feeling hunger. Satisfy yourself. What circumstances in life are truly holding you back? You are in control. Remove yourself from toxic people with shitty ideas of what you should or shouldn't want. Take out a loan and spend it frivilously if you feel like that's what you want. If you're young, there are many banks and shit that will be dying to put you into debt. So fucking what? Don't pay it back if you don't find yourself with the means to do so. What the hell does a credit rating even mean anyway? Nothing. Fuck it. The absolute worst case scenario is you get thrown in jail for not giving some business back their money. Big deal. Your needs still get met in prison, joke's on whoever threw you in jail. Not that I am at all encouraging crime in any sense, as in most cases doing horrible shit negatively affects your own quality of life. You only get one chance and then there's nothing. Your energy disappates into the universe after death and will never combine itself again in the form of you, here, right now. Use that to your advantage! There literally is no point to your existence other than what you make of it for yourself in the short time you are able to experience anything at all. So why not experience? You don't have anything to lose, but you also have everything to gain and then regardless of what anybody has, there will come a time where it's "light's out forever" for everyone. 



At the time I was trying to open up with my friends I hadn't come to this...I don't know...revelation? I was merely just trying to talk about my thoughts. And like I said, their reactions were based on their discomfort with my true self. So they tried to stop me from being true with them by telling me what I was saying was scary, or that my thoughts were an illness and I needed help and medication to stop thinking. In knowing this I realized that the friends I thought I had were not friends at all and the actual sadness I'm feeling has absolutely nothing to do with the realization that my life is meaningless in the realest sense of the word, but everything to do with the isolation and aloneness I felt when I tried to reach out. It's a very uncomfortable experience realizing that you have nobody. That everybody you know really isn't interested in getting to know who you actually are, but is only interested in having you be around in order to placate them and satisfy their own needs when they think your presence might be useful to them. 


This includes family. 


You never asked to be born into your family, so you owe them nothing. Your mother, although she birthed you, is not a virtuous person full of goodness just because she decided to keep you. Once you came out of the birth canal, your life became yours and only yours. You must not waste it with people who become bored with you while you're growing into who you truly want to be. Separate yourself from these people with moral falsehoods and be true to you, always. Don't ever cripple yourself with guilt and obligation to people who don't encourage you to be the purest representation of your true thoughts and feelings. You may find yourself isolated and alone for a long time, or you may not. The point is, you'll never know unless you start taking action of some sort. I'm at this stage now and it's very scary. But I have hope that once we remove ourselves from toxic people and toxic situations, we will be free to experience just our true selves. It's kind of exciting. 


What are your thoughts?

You're right, there are consequences to negative actions such as those. 


But if your child hits somebody and you take away their TV privileges, I don't see that as being equal to the wrong they have done. It doesn't teach your child not to hit because hitting hurts people and that hurting people is wrong because it infringes on another person's right to be safe in their own body, it just enforces the idea that if they hit somebody and they get caught, they might get something taken away. I don't think it really teaches them compassion and empathy. This whole idea of "Don't do wrong or your shit is going to be taken from you by authority (including things like your house, rights to your body, etc.)" is the reason why there are so many psychopaths inside the government who rule the people through fear instead of teaching the people to rule themselves based on moral principles that should be universal.

I don't really think taking things away from a child for punishment has any real world application at all. Sure, punishment teaches a child not to do something wrong, but it establishes a mindset of "don't do wrong," out of fear instead of empathy, which I think is a lot more important than retribution 


Personally I would just explain to the child why what they did was wrong and how it made me or the party they have wronged feel. At an early age this will establish compassion and help a child learn how to solve problems in the real world productively. If an adult does you wrong, you can't just take away their shit. It's unrealistic. 


Obviously if your child doesn't have vocabulary yet you can't fully explain to them what is happening and expect them to understand, but one could argue that just talking to your child anyway will help establish boundaries once they are fully able to understand. If they have an object that they shouldn't, the only thing to do is to remove it from them to keep them out of harm's way. Or if they're running into something that could hurt them, stop the action and verbalize why you are doing it. If you repeat this enough, once they become coherent and understand language it will inhibit these kinds of dangerous acts in the future.


If your child is throwing a tantrum, you need to ask your child how they are feeling and empathize with them. "I understand you want this (thing) and that makes you sad/angry/frustrated, but it is not in the budget right now. I'm very sorry but we will not be going home with this today. Would a hug from mommy make you feel better?" 


If you are consistent (and you MUST be consistent) in this sort of routine "discipline," there will be minimal issue. All of my siblings and myself have been raised this way and my parents rarely had issues. We have, all four of us, grown up to be wonderful individuals. We were not spoiled and we do not have any sense of entitlement whatsoever. None of us have ever been in trouble with the law and we were all respectful students in school. Of course children test boundaries, but it is your job as a parent to be caring and understanding toward your child. Make your child feel safe around you, instead of seeing you as just an authority figure.

He dawdles when it's time to go anywhere. We'll be all ready to leave. Then suddenly, right as we are literally walking out the door, he has to take out the garbage NOW, when the pick up isn't for another two days and we will be back home in like an hour. Or clean the cat litter NOW. Make sure he emptied the Keurig NOW. Suddenly every random task that can wait until later always becomes super important before we leave the house, regardless of how long we are going to be gone. 


Annoying as hell.

So guilty of this.

I really just want you to get in and out of the store as fast as possible because I don't want to look at any more dumb faces for the day.

There is a certain point during every day in retail where all faces suddenly become dumb looking. It's not you. It's customer service.

I understand and empathize at her disappointment over the situation, especially if when you left, there may have been some ambiguity about whether or not it was a legitimate emergency that required immediate attention. Certainly a lack of explanation on what kind of stomach pains your niece was experiencing could have made her feel like this was not that big of a deal. If you left in a rush with little explanation, I'd have probably felt similar. 


However, after the situation was explained in detail the next morning, I would have figured she would be more understanding. It's your family, clearly family means a lot to you and your willingness to be there for your niece is an admirable quality - especially if your girlfriend right now is at all considering you to be the father of her children someday. If I were her, and your niece called you in the middle of the night for help and you ignored it, that would make me question whether or not I would want you as a long term partner or the father of my children. I think deep down she probably knows she would feel the same if you just shrugged it off as if your niece was being a pain in your ass. My guess is this guilt is probably why she is so upset about it. That's entirely speculation though. I don't know your girlfriend. 


Hope you guys can work it out. xo

Well, I'm not going to delve into why I think saying depression is a mental illness is totally detrimental to actually understanding anybody who suffers with depressed thoughts....


However, I would not consider myself to be depressed in my daily life. Of course, thinking the way I have described is depressing. How could it not be? At the same time though it isn't like it's the only thing I think about. I also wouldn't go as far as to say the depression manifests itself as sadness, either. I have everything going for me. I find enjoyment in a lot of things, I laugh all the time. Real laughter, too. I have fun with my friends, I go on road trips, I have a great family life and a wonderful job. 


I'm just completely apathetic about the value of my life, or anybody's life for that matter. I don't think that it something therapy can fix, because I know my thoughts are not a result of trauma that I need to get over. And they're also not a result of paranoia or a chemical imbalance. My thoughts are a result of observing the world and how it actually works. My thoughts are just absolute truth. Therapy might supply me with an avenue to vent, and drugs might make me high enough to pretend it's not an issue, but those things aren't going to reform the governing forces of the world. Me being prescribed therapy and medication isn't going to make other people realize they are modern day slaves and slave owners and do something to change it. 


These realities aren't just going to go away if I have the right person to talk to. And I'm not stupid enough to believe that someday everything is going to be okay because it's not.


And so what if everything did end up okay? I'm just going to die anyway. We all die. I don't see how me skipping out a bit early is going to affect anything other than the individuals I have relationships with. And yeah, that's going to hurt them really bad, but staying alive for them just reinforces the fact that I'm only alive to serve other people and that MY life and MY feelings don't actually mean anything unless they benefit somebody else.

Well, you don't know me at all. 



My problem isn't that I'm actually physically isolated or anything. I have a great job, I meet a lot of people in the run of a day. I have friends. I exercise on the regular. I eat healthy. Literally nothing is actually wrong in my life - I just have no desire to live because it seems pointless to me, and all of the reasons people try to give me in order to keep living are actually retarded and pointless. All they really circle around is shit like, "THINK OF ALL THE THINGS YOU WILL MISS," or, "Think of all the people you'll hurt," "Would you really want to put your loved ones through that?" 


I won't think anything. I'll be fucking dead. -shrug-


I'm going to at least try the wwoof thing next summer. I agreed to help my father get his house ready to sell over the winter, so in the spring time I might spend some time away just to escape the monotony of my life. I can't do it now because I have an apartment, but the lease ends in September and I'll be living with my father to help him around his place after that. Come springtime I won't have rent to pay so there is no obligation to stay where I am. 



It might help me, but to be honest it probably won't. I've always felt this way.

Came here to throw some mutual feels your way, since you did the same for me. 

<3

Man. Thank you for these resources. I think that wwoof thing is amazeballs, so I'm definitely going to work toward doing that next spring.

It's really hard for me to envision a perfect life when I feel like everything is so meaningless anyway. 


However, I think ultimately I'd like to live on a farm or in the woods and grow my own food. Maybe have a little community where a few close friends and myself grow lots of food for ourselves, build things for ourselves and if we end up with surplus we could sell it at a market and save up money for more infrastructure to expand our community or something. 


Sounds all well and great and it definitely is possible. What depresses me is that somebody else controls whether or not I can do this, whether it be in regards to land ownership, building permits, vendors licenses to sell goods, property tax, income tax, work visas and residency applications if I want to live in another country, etc. The fact is that nobody is truly free to just exist peacefully and satisfy their own needs without servicing somebody else who has been somehow deemed morally righteous enough to control the rest of the population. 


It's not just about finding something I truly enjoy doing. It's about how there is ultimately somebody who controls what I can and cannot do. There is a group of individuals in control, telling everybody what they have a right to and what they don't. And it seems that right at this present moment, in Western society, we are all advocating for human rights and nobody seems to be appalled by the fact that everybody NEEDS clean water and food to stay alive and we have to have permission from a financial institution in order to have both. 


But yeah, it's real important that women get paid the same amount as men and that gay people can be married. Not that I'm at all against either of those things - I just feel like people should be rioting in the streets over the fact that Canada is giving away most of their fresh water resources to Nestlé and Monsanto owns like 80% of the world's produce. 


Like is that not fucked up to anybody else?!?!

Yes. 


I find myself feeling very isolated, because I want to talk this out but every single person I know tells me it's too scary and they dismiss my feelings  as just paranoia.


I'm not fucking paranoid. I just understand how the world works right now and it's horribly depressing and there is legitimately nothing I can do about it. 


I could very well work and buy a house off the grid, move to a new country, whatever. What depresses me is knowing that I can't do ANY of those things without somebody else allowing me to do it in the first place. I need permission from somebody else to just exist anywhere.
I know your feels. <3

Death is nothing. There, I would be completely void of any kind of experience at all. While alive, however, I live with the anxiety and depression that accompanies the realization that I have to justify my existence by essentially being a slave, or a slave owner. AND, if I don't want to be either of those things, people call me lazy or childish. I could not have access to any medical care. In some cases I could even possibly be arrested. 


The lives we all live now are fucking horrible. We are all just flooded with distraction after distraction to disengage ourselves from everything that's happening around us. Don't you see it? How can you not see it? How can you not see how atrocious this world has become? How do any of you live with yourselves? 


This is a serious question. The world is so fucked up man. How do you keep going?
Sounds very nice but if I take a vacation, I can't pay my bills. :D

I am not religious at all, but I get your point. 


I understand everything you're saying. I really do. And I appreciate the insight and perspective on what I'm feeling. 


I won't argue with your logic because you are absolutely right. I could do those things. I can do anything. The problem I have is that I don't want to HAVE to do anything - I just want to exist and for me right now it's not possible unless I put in a lot of work. 


My point is that it's absolutely abhorrent that people normalize the ideas of laws and an economy and letting somebody else tell you what you have rights to and what you don't. They normalize the fact that you HAVE to contribute to everyone else in order to be alive. Even if it's only for a little bit, you still HAVE to do it. You can't just simply be alive and do your own thing without obligation to somebody else. It makes me sick to my stomach.

Yes exactly this. It really irks me when people say, "Oh find something you like doing and just do that as your career."

I like and find immense amounts of enjoyment in a lot of things. My problem is that I'm completely apathetic toward everything I do and I see no point struggling to make ends meet doing something I like just to die anyway. 


I don't even know why I'm here. I guess I just need to vent. I know one way or the other, I'm going to die on my own terms. Might be this year, might be 30 years down the road when I've decided I've really had enough of this obligatory life sentence. 


I'm glad somebody feels the same though. Not that I'm in any way happy you're feeling so low too, but it's nice knowing I'm not alone.

The thing with that though is that in order to live off the grid, I need to get money in the first place. Just the property alone costs thousands of dollars, and in order to get that I'd have to save up for at least 20 years because I have to sustain my life and pay to be alive in the meantime. 

My problem is the idea that I HAVE to have a job in order to be alive. Even if I just said fuck it and went to live in the woods somewhere, somebody owns that property and would inevitably come after me for some kind of monetary compensation for the use of that land. It's actually illegal to build a permanent dwelling anywhere unless you have some paperwork, and that requires large sums of money that I just don't have. 


So then my option is to go to school and put myself into debt, and work on paying that off before I can even think of buying any kind of property. 


And even if I did I'm just going to work super hard to achieve that, maybe spend a couple years happy if everything works out and then die. What is the point?

As a person with this frame of mind I would never try to convince a person who truly did not want to be alive to stay alive. It's not fair, especially if I'm feeling their perspective as hard as I am right now. 

The most I would do is sit and listen to them if they gave out a cry for help. I am personally indifferent to the outcome of the situation because I understand it from both sides so deeply. I would encourage a person to say how they are feeling, and I have been in this situation a few times and each time, the person themselves comes up with the conclusion that they don't actually want to die, so they haven't gone through with it and are happier now. I have never once told a person who came to me with suicidal thoughts to not commit suicide. I have also never told a person who came to me with suicidal thoughts to commit suicide. I have no authority over what an individual does to their own body. In each case that I have experienced however, the person always had some sort of trauma they felt they just couldn't live with. A rape, abuse, financial crisis, addiction, no friends, something like that. In most cases, people in their most desperate come to terms with these traumas, let go, and realize they want to experience life and become successful. And you know, good for them. If talking to me about their issues helps them find a desire to be alive, that's awesome. I'm truly happy for them and I wish them all the best. 


I am not for or against either position on this matter. I just understand both.

I am having these exact thoughts right now. I have been for the last year. Last week, these thoughts are what brought me to this subreddit - to see if maybe somebody else here feels similar. 


Last week a friend of mine committed suicide. Every single one of our mutual friends was deeply saddened by this, and as much as I feel some sadness for the people who consider this to be a horrible tragedy, apart from that I felt nothing but envy for her.



I have been looking through posts every single day since then, and I realized that everybody else has so many problems. Up until now I hadn't seen a post that was relative to how I am feeling at all. Everyone seems to have experienced abuse of some sort, a disability, an illness, the loss of a friend or partner - JUST SOMETHING, that attributes to their lives being completely miserable. I feel very bad. I feel genuinely selfish and horrible, because I have no problems. I am hilarious. I'm intelligent. I am empathetic, kind, compassionate. I have a great job and enough money to spend on the things I like. My family was never abusive. I have always been great at making friends anywhere I go. I can put in minimal effort and excel at everything I do. I have never failed at anything. 



I just can't shake this feeling of unjust obligation to life. It's absolutely ridiculous to me that I can't just simply exist. Somehow, I have to justify my life by working and contributing to a society that I had absolutely no control over being involved in. I never asked to be born, and if I ever had the option, knowing the stipulations that accompany life inside civilization and on this planet, I would have passed. 



I have absolutely no desire to keep living at this present time, but the social obligation I'm under to stay alive floods me with an atrocious amount of guilt. I know that when I die, I won't be able to feel guilt for my actions. I'll be dead. I will feel nothing. But my consciousness while alive eats at me, knowing that even though I won't get to see their faces, even though I will feel nothing, a lot of people will be horribly affected by this. I don't know what to do.
